context: Owner decision 2026-11-17: Q21 capture runs on GitHub-hosted Linux runners (16 GB) with the server container limited to 5.25 GiB, so the release envelope stays the same.
description:
## Problem
In the 2026-11-12 tuning evidence (PR #4191, _project/analysis/clickhouse-tuning-evidence-sf1/), TPC-H Q21 failed in all four arms (notuning, A/A copy, layout-only, full tuned) on ClickHouse 25.8.33.6 under the macOS 27 Mocker path with a 5.25 GiB guest limit, so every TPC-H SF1 ClickHouse verdict covers 21 of 22 queries. PR #4162 already applies a statement-level join_algorithm for Q21 in all modes as a harness requirement; Q21 still fails. No tracker item owns this; clickhouse-server-tpcds-q10-memory-20261008 is the TPC-DS analogue.

## Decision gate
Capture the failure first: error code and message, peak memory from system.query_log, and the join algorithm actually used. Then:
- If a ClickHouse setting (spill, join algorithm, max_bytes_before_external_*) lets Q21 finish within 5.25 GiB in every mode, declare it as a harness requirement the way #4162 did (applied in all modes, recorded per query), not as tuning. Change or extend the existing Q21 entry (join_algorithm=hash) in benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/statement_settings.py; do not add a second one.
- If Q21 needs more memory than the release envelope, record a documented envelope reason that cites the measured peak, and keep it out of verdict denominators explicitly.
- If ClickHouse returns a wrong result or crashes, file it as an engine defect with a reproducer.

## Guardrails
- Q21 must return the reference row count wherever it is reported as passing.
- No change that applies only to the tuned arm (that would bias the benefit rule).
- Runs go through make heavy-run; see heavy-work-host-capacity-owner-decision-20261117 if the host cannot hold them.
